clue.text: Fluid duct drained, fixed in advance

indicators.note: fluid means flowing and changeable, so the letters of the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A plumber notes a pipe has been emptied of water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fluid' looks like the liquid in the duct, but it signals that DUCT DRAINED is to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a matter settled beforehand, with no room left for discussion, is said to be this.

clue.text: Reticent to swallow drop of liquid? It's producing flatulence

indicators.note: one word taking in another, as a mouth swallows food, so the second piece goes inside

parts.note: reticent means shy, or coy
a lick is a small amount, as in a lick of paint

explanation.surface: A shy person wonders whether gulping some drink brings on wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Colic is gut pain often accompanied by wind, so something colicky brings on gas.

clue.text: Time to get foul-mouthed briefly, being in the clan

indicators.note: a word cut short loses its final letter

parts.note: ribald means coarse and vulgar in speech

explanation.surface: Someone joins a group and starts swearing for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: Tribal describes what belongs to a tribe, a close kin group much like a clan.

clue.text: Man on board reportedly not heavy — a wicked type in the dark?

definitions.text: a wicked type in the dark?

indicators.note: as reported, so what is said aloud matters, not the spelling

parts.note: a knight is a chess piece, a man on the chessboard
something not heavy is light

explanation.surface: A chess piece is apparently not weighty, and a villain lurks in darkness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wicked' is a pun: the answer is a candle-type lamp with a wick, burning in the dark.
explanation.definitionFit: A small lamp left burning through the night; the old kind was a candle with a wick, hence 'wicked'.

clue.text: Daughter hugged by proper dandy

indicators.note: being hugged puts one piece inside the arms of the other

parts.note: due means fitting or proper, as in due respect

explanation.surface: A daughter is embraced by a correctly dressed man of fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both name a man very concerned with his clothes and appearance.

clue.text: Uneducated drunk ranting about nothing

indicators.note: going about something surrounds it, so one piece holds the other
drunk suggests something reeling and jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: O is the zero-shaped letter for nothing

explanation.surface: An unschooled drunkard rants on about nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges RANTING into IGNRANT, and 'about' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone lacking schooling or knowledge is described as unlearned in this way.

clue.text: Goddess encountered in grass, rolling over

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other
turned over, so the word for grass is written backwards

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass of wet places
met means encountered

explanation.surface: A goddess is met with lying in long grass, rolling about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rolling over' turns REED round to DEER; 'in' sets MET inside. The grass she rolls in fits a harvest goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: She is the Greek goddess of the harvest and grain, mother of Persephone.

clue.text: Form of advertisement bad, put in rubbish container, not much good

indicators.note: one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: a bin holds rubbish
ill means bad, as in ill effects

indicators.note: only a little of the next word, its first letter

explanation.surface: A poor advert gets thrown in the bin as useless.
explanation.definitionFit: Billing is publicity, the way performers are listed and promoted on posters, as in top billing.

clue.text: Mistake over kiss? One would have been shot!

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places the first piece above the second

parts.note: a blunder is a mistake
buss is an old word for a kiss

explanation.surface: An error in kissing someone could get a person shot.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: this old firearm would have been fired, so 'shot', in its day.
explanation.definitionFit: An old short-barrelled musket with a flared muzzle; such guns were fired, so one would have been shot.

clue.text: Police department brings in lots — all about to become vigorous

indicators.note: the whole thing is turned about, so it is read backwards
one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police
many means lots

explanation.surface: Detectives make many arrests and become energetic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brings in' makes CIMANYD, and 'all about' turns the whole of it backwards. CID is Britain's plain-clothes detective branch.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: full of energy and drive, forceful and active.

clue.text: Is lady able to travel round and see tailless bird?

parts.note: read as the question 'can Ada?', is a lady named Ada able
to go is to travel
O is round in shape

indicators.note: without its tail, so the last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a woman can go on a trip to see a bird with no tail.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a large North American waterfowl with a black neck, now common in Britain too.

clue.text: Pick out some in bunch as terrorists, immoral

indicators.note: some letters within the next words are picked out, a run hiding inside them

explanation.surface: Select a few from a group of terrorists, who are wicked.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking chastity, sexually immoral or impure.

clue.text: Soft corrosion on something tiny

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for soft
rot is decay or corrosion

explanation.surface: Mild rust appears on a small object.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a subatomic particle in the nucleus, about as tiny as things get.

clue.text: Little fellow with one stone in battle ultimately accounting for him?

definitions.text: Little fellow with one stone in battle ultimately accounting for him?

parts.note: Phil is a short form of the name Philip
I is the Roman numeral for one
ST is the abbreviation for stone, the weight

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: David, a small man with a single stone, kills a giant in battle.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue tells of David killing Goliath with one sling stone; Goliath was a Philistine.
explanation.definitionFit: Goliath, the giant felled by young David's slingshot, belonged to this biblical people.

clue.text: Periods of hold-ups with elevated railroad sealed off

indicators.note: something sealed off is cut out, so letters are removed

parts.note: delays are hold-ups
the EL is an American elevated railway, as in Chicago

explanation.surface: Times of waiting while an overhead railway is closed.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym in the sense of eras or times, as in 'in my younger days'.

clue.text: Pole swinging close by flower?

parts.note: a flower is a river, something that flows; an angler swings a pole beside it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is a crossword trick: a river is something that flows. 'Pole' is not a Polish person.
explanation.definitionFit: An angler casts this long rod, swinging it out beside a river.

clue.text: Divert a short distance round overturned vehicle

indicators.note: one piece goes round the other, enclosing it
cut short, so the word loses its ending to leave the usual abbreviation

parts.note: taken as written before cutting

indicators.note: turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a cart is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Take a small detour around an upturned wagon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts DISTANCE to DIST; 'overturned' turns CART into TRAC, which 'round' encloses. The 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to draw someone's attention away, to sidetrack them.

clue.text: Teacher comes to fancy hotel — a place for buns

parts.note: a rabbi is a Jewish religious teacher

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or fanciful, so the next word is rearranged

explanation.surface: A teacher turns up at a luxury hotel known for its bakery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buns' is bunnies, rabbits, not bread rolls.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbit's burrow is where bunnies live, so a home for buns in that sense.

clue.text: English town has plot to get car manufacturer

parts.note: a bed is a garden plot, as in a flowerbed
Ford is an American car maker

explanation.surface: An English town's land is bought by a car maker.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: it is the county town of Bedfordshire, north of London.

clue.text: Get a divining rod

definitions.meaning: informal British: to understand, to get it
a forked stick used by dowsers to find water

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a dowser's forked stick, and slang for grasping a point.

clue.text: Walter's terrible idler

indicators.note: something terrible is in a bad state, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: the name with its S, all seven letters used

explanation.surface: Walter is a dreadful layabout.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the S of Walter's counts as a letter of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a good-for-nothing who wastes time and money, a loafer.

clue.text: Cold artist against a tie — that is unwanted item of neckwear

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
V is versus, against

indicators.note: the named letters are not wanted, so taken out

parts.note: taken as written
IE is id est, that is

explanation.surface: A chilly painter objects to wearing a tie he does not want.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a wide scarf-like band worn round the neck, an ancestor of the necktie.

clue.text: Latest report to give time when Oxford term will start?

definitions.meaning: a bulletin bringing news up to date

definitions.text: time when Oxford term will start?
definitions.meaning: students 'go up' to Oxford, so the date of going up

explanation.walkthrough: Students are said to go 'up' to Oxford; the second reading is UP DATE, the day they go up.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulletin with the newest information, and whimsically the day students go up to university.

clue.text: Coffee offering energy, thus crowd's imbibed

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: drunk in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: so means thus
a press is a crowd or throng

explanation.surface: Coffee gives a boost, so the crowd drinks it up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imbibed' signals the container: the crowd word sits inside ESO. 'Press' as crowd is the older sense, a throng.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a strong black coffee made by forcing steam through ground beans.

clue.text: One in street sharing something with a neighbour

definitions.text: One in street sharing something with a neighbour

parts.words: One in street sharing something with a neighbour
parts.note: a house in a street that shares a wall with the next-door house

explanation.walkthrough: The 'something' shared is a party wall; British houses built in joined pairs are common.
explanation.definitionFit: British short form for a semi-detached house, joined to its neighbour by one wall.

clue.text: Men on street taking time to find safe accommodation

indicators.note: in an across clue, on places the first piece after the second

parts.note: OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Soldiers in the street take a while to find secure lodging.
explanation.definitionFit: A place where goods are kept securely, a safe space for keeping things.

clue.text: Fashionable to have very limited language? The opposite

parts.note: in means fashionable
V is the short form of very
Erse is the Gaelic language of Ireland or Scotland

explanation.surface: Is it trendy to speak with hardly any words? Quite the reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something turned the other way, its reverse or contrary.

clue.text: Awfully tired intellectual becomes harmful

indicators.note: awfully means in a terrible way, so the next word's letters are jumbled

parts.note: mental means of the mind, intellectual

explanation.surface: A worn-out thinker becomes damaging.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: causing damage or loss, as in detrimental to health.
